title: Site-definition store: supersede not-found message unification (DB-040 s) - the last known store oracle, mirroring the accepted T067 revoke fix
objective: Close DB-040(s), the G5-LOW-1 the M5-T067 security review surfaced with a reproduction (M5-T067-G5.md): supersede's not-found branches still emit divergent text - the missing-record branch echoes the probed id while the existing-but-foreign branch returns distinct static text, and the supersedes_id-mismatch branch is a third divergent message that fires only when the record exists. Unify ALL not-found-class supersede refusal messages to identical text with NO id echo, mirroring the accepted revoke unification byte-for-byte in discipline: same exception class, same refusal code, byte-identical message across the missing and foreign branches; the supersedes_id-mismatch branch must either share that identical text or be proven to fire identically for missing and existing records (no existence signal either way). Store-level and route-level equality tests mirroring the accepted T067 pair; mutation-sensitive both ways; every legitimate same-property path byte-preserved; the scope-before-status order and insert guards UNTOUCHED.
business_reason: The security sweep says this is the last known existence oracle in the store - closing it now means the record substrate goes into the future mount/auth work oracle-free
inputs: CHECKPOINT ENVELOPE (binding): in every checkpoint, OMIT the four envelope fields entirely - the controller fills them. If you supply one it must be EXACT full-length (40-hex SHA, FULL worktree path).

REPORT DISCIPLINE (binding): reference files and line anchors, never embed long verbatim sections; the [OBSERVED]/[BLOCKED]/[PREDICTED] evidence-status form the accepted T067 report used is the standard - route what you cannot run to harvest, never fake it.

COMMAND CWD (binding): api work runs from services/api - `python -m ruff check .` FIRST, then the documented pytest; `python tools/modularity_check.py --check` from repo root. KNOWN BROKER LIMIT: documented commands run from the worktree root, so the scoped pytest may be [BLOCKED] for you - route it to harvest exactly as T067 did.

SPEC SOURCE (binding): project-control/reports/M5-T067-G5.md finding G5-LOW-1 (verbatim text + reproduction recipe) and the accepted revoke unification in the same store (the (r) fix, M5-T067 material) - mirror its discipline exactly. The scope-before-status order (the accepted (q) fix) and the _record_insert guards are FROZEN behavior: your diff must not reorder any check, only unify message text (and remove id echoes).

CODE-GRAPH NAVIGATION BLOCK (D-066-R001; graph regenerated this session: 793/16728/7304): store.py consumers = the routes (api/v1/, FORBIDDEN) + condo_records read path (FORBIDDEN); consumer-sweep duty: no out-of-scope suite pins the old supersede message texts - verify by grep and report; if one does, STOP and report the exact assertion (never edit out-of-scope tests).

BEHAVIOR PRESERVATION (binding): the ONLY observable change is supersede's not-found-class message text (unified, no id echo); every status/state/refusal-code pair byte-identical; the existing 74 scoped tests stay green unchanged (adjusting only assertions that pin the OLD supersede message texts, each named in the report).
outputs: Oracle-free supersede messages (unified not-found-class text, no id echo), mutation-tested at store and route level
acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (unification): supersede's missing-record and existing-but-foreign probes return byte-identical exception class, refusal code, AND message text, with neither echoing the probed id - direct equality assertions at store level and route level (full-body equality minus correlation_id), mirroring the accepted revoke pair.

AS-2 (third branch): the supersedes_id-mismatch refusal either shares the identical not-found text or is proven by test to respond identically for missing and existing records - no existence signal from any supersede refusal.
AS-3 (mutation sensitivity): diverging any unified literal, or reintroducing an id echo, turns a test red.

AS-4 (frozen order): the scope-before-status order and the insert guards are byte-untouched - the diff contains no reordering; the accepted T067 tests (foreign-probe 404 across all three statuses; own-record 409; after==before) stay green unchanged.
AS-5 (preservation): full scoped suite green; any adjusted pre-existing assertion pins only the OLD supersede message text and is named in the report; ruff clean; modularity exit 0.
risks: The supersedes_id-mismatch branch fires before the scope check - unifying its text versus proving response-identity are different designs; the producer chooses and JUSTIFIES one in the report (the packet accepts either, AS-2).
Message-text assertions may exist pinning the old supersede texts - the consumer-sweep duty routes out-of-scope hits to the orchestrator.
This packet must not touch ordering: a reorder = scope violation even if tests stay green.
